comment: The upstream revision every corpus rule came from. `tools/import-cxx.py --all --pin tests/corpus/PIN.json --git-repo <llvm> --check` must reproduce every .gisel file byte for byte. The commit is a plain upstream llvm-project commit: local patches in a worktree cannot change what was imported, so the corpus keeps the reviewed deviations below. `patches` lists the upstream PRs carried on top of `commit` (unmerged, or merged after `commit`); the official side of the A/B harness is built from a tree with them applied, which is why the corpus asks for the post-fix behaviour. When they land upstream, move `commit` past them and delete both the patches and the deviations.

patches.title: [GlobalISel] Keep the lane count in maxScalarEltSameAsIf
[X86][GlobalISel] Don't widen G_BUILD_VECTOR to legalize it
[X86][GlobalISel] Mark vector G_CTPOP legal when VPOPCNT is available
[GlobalISel] Pick a sub-register result class that has the value type
[TableGen] Diagnose !head/!tail of a deferred empty list

official_base.comment: The official side of the A/B harness is frozen here. `files` is the sha256 of every file whose content can change a legalizer answer, taken from the exact tree the official library was built from. ab/check-pin.sh compares content, not ancestry: a tree passes only if all of these match. Changing any of them is a baseline change -- rebuild, re-run every direction of evidence, and update this map in the same commit. Do not edit the tree and leave the map behind.

frozen.note: The corpus is imported from `import_commit`; the rule sources below are that commit plus the declared patches plus the three declared local deviations. The pin-only tree is reproducible with pin/make-base.sh and is a cross-check, not the baseline: the generated constructor needs the `core*` builders that live only in this tree's LegalizerInfo.h.

deviations.effect: numElements() spells out the release-build answer (0) for scalar element counts instead of asserting. The rule text is unchanged; an assertions build now answers the scalar queries a release build would. This is the one local change that can change an official answer.

memSizeInBytesNotPow2() reads the known minimum of a scalable TypeSize instead of the fatal implicit conversion. No target in this tree references that predicate, so it cannot change an official answer; it still has to be declared because the file's bytes differ from the pin.

Adds the core* builders (coreMinScalarSameAs, coreClampNumElements, ...) that the generated constructor calls. Methods only, no data members, and no upstream constructor calls them, so the official library's answers are unchanged; the additions exist because the generated include cannot be compiled against a pin-only header.
